Question: Has the CA Owner disclosed in CCADB every subordinate CA certificate in this hierarchy, including any not logged to Certificate Transparency?
Does the CA Owner publicly disclose all compliance incidents within 24 hours of discovery?
In the last 2 years, has the CA Owner had no repeated incidents of a similar kind?
In the last 2 years, has the CA Owner been free of incidents that pre-issuance linting would have caught?

Can the CA Owner enumerate and analyze its entire valid-certificate population (for example, to identify every certificate affected by an incident) using only its own systems, without relying on external sources such as crt.sh or Censys?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented incident-response command structure that names a role with authority to halt issuance and command revocation?
Has the CA Owner contributed at least one public comment to a Bugzilla incident report owned by another CA Owner in the past 2 years?
Does the CA Owner's incident root-cause analysis identify all contributing factors, not only the immediate cause?

In the last 3 years, did the CA Owner avoid having an audit finding (a qualification, exception, nonconformity, or material weakness) that it fixed and closed during the audit period, so it did not appear on the final audit report?
In the last 2 years, has the CA Owner been free of any outdated-audit-statement reminder from CCADB?
Does the CA Owner document in the CP/CPS the trust purpose served by each Root CA Certificate in this hierarchy (as defined in the Apple Root Program Policy)?
Are the CA Owner's policy documents each scoped to a single Trust Purpose (a single CP/CPS may cover multiple hierarchies that share the same Trust Purpose)?
Does the CA Owner record every pre-issuance linting decision (block, advisory, or override) to its issuance audit trail?
Does the CA Owner operate an internal PKI compliance function that is organizationally independent from operations?
Does the CA Owner comply with each new industry-standard requirement by its effective date?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented process for tracking changes to CA/B Forum, Apple Root Program, and CCADB requirements?
Are all certificate profiles documented in the relevant CP/CPS, including all fields and properties in use?
Does the CA Owner document in the CP/CPS the geographic regions from which it accepts Subscribers?
Does the CA Owner state in its CP/CPS that it does not use publicly-trusted hierarchies for enterprise-only or locally-trusted use cases, and that it offers separate private hierarchies for those?

Does the CA Owner describe policies and practices for this hierarchy in a single combined CP/CPS authored in Markdown format and free-standing (does not require external policy documents to interpret)?
Does the CA Owner document in the CP/CPS the geographic regions where its CA infrastructure operates (key-holding, signing, and certificate-status systems)?
Does the CA Owner document in the CP/CPS its use (or non-use) of cross-certification between Root CA generations?
Does the CA Owner follow a formal compliance or risk-management framework (such as ISO 27001 or NIST 800-53) that has been operational for at least 2 years?
Does the CA Owner limit the maximum age of key material used for Root CA Certificates to 15 years or less?
Does the CA Owner verify at least annually that complete cradle-to-grave records (including all key-signing ceremony records) exist for every Root CA in this hierarchy?
Does the CA Owner maintain sole control over all CA key material in this hierarchy?
Does the CA Owner generate and store CA private keys in FIPS 140-2 (or 140-3) Level 3 or higher certified hardware operating in a Level 3 or higher compliant mode?
Does the CA Owner intend to sign replacement Root CA Certificates at least 2 years before current Root expiration and submit them to the Apple Root Program at least 18 months before production use?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented process to transition to replacement signature, hash, or key-establishment algorithms when a cryptographic algorithm in use is found to be weakened or broken?

By 2030-12-31, will every Root CA hierarchy the CA Owner has in the Apple Root Program serve only one Trust Purpose? The CA Owner may reach this by retiring or replacing any hierarchy that serves more than one today.
Does the CA Owner avoid placing any non-Apple Trust Purpose (such as Document Signing, IoT, or Time Stamping) on a Root CA hierarchy that also serves an Apple Trust Purpose?
Does the CA Owner intend to generate new Root CA certificates at least every 5 years?
Does the CA Owner migrate issuance from one Root CA generation to the next at least every 7 years?
Does the CA Owner require zero issuance from a deprecated Root CA for at least 12 months before requesting its removal from the Apple Root Program?
Does the CA Owner ensure no unexpired leaf certificates (except test certificates) chain to a deprecated Root CA before requesting its removal?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented Root CA certificate replacement process including the trigger criteria for replacement?
Is every CA certificate in this hierarchy operated by the CA Owner itself, with no Externally-Operated Subordinate CA run by a separate legal entity?
Does the CA Owner commit not to delegate any subordinate CA in this hierarchy to a separate legal entity in the future without Apple approval?
Does the CA Owner operate this hierarchy without External Registration Authorities (RAs)?

For every Externally-Operated Subordinate CA and every inbound cross-signed CA certificate in this hierarchy that may exist, is pathLenConstraint set to 0, so the external operator cannot issue further subordinate CA certificates?
Does the CA Owner cap subordinate CA certificate validity at 3 years or less (Apple's target)?
Does the CA Owner cap subordinate CA certificate validity at 5 years or less (Apple's maximum)?
Does the CA Owner run weak-key and known-bad-key detection (such as badkeys, pwnedkeys, ROCA, and Debian weak keys) at issuance and block issuance on a hit?

Does the CA Owner lint every pre-sign certificate before attempting pre-certificate or final certificate issuance with at least one industry-recognized tool (such as pkilint, zlint, x509lint, or Cablint)?
Does linting block issuance when it finds an error?
Does the CA Owner run its own post-issuance linting across all valid certificates, rather than relying on external CT-log monitoring (such as crt.sh) as a substitute?
Does the CA Owner perform documented manual content review for semantic errors that automated linting cannot catch (such as organization-name accuracy in organization-validated certificates)?
Does the CA Owner's linting scope extend beyond subscriber certificates to CRLs and ARLs and to subordinate CA certificates?

Does the CA Owner perform post-issuance linting on all valid certificates (pre-certificates or final certificates) with detection latency of 24 hours or less and maintain a documented severity-prioritized remediation process?
If the CA Owner disables any lints, are the disabled lints, the disabling rationale, and the per-lint applicability justification fully documented?
Does the CA Owner operate at least two distinct linting tools (defense in depth)?
Does the CA Owner refresh its weak-key and known-bad-key dataset at least every 90 days?
Does the CA Owner currently perform certificate linting (pre-issuance, post-issuance, or both)?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented investigation, escalation, and trend-tracking process for pre-issuance linting failures?
Does the CA Owner deploy updates to its linting tools within 90 days of upstream release, after testing in a staging environment?
In the last 2 years, has the CA Owner avoided any unauthorized issuance or mis-issuance event?
Does the CA Owner test at least annually that it can revoke all active certificates within 24 hours in case of a mass-revocation event?
Does the CA Owner have processes to identify and revoke all misissued certificates and commit to revoke within the timelines required by applicable industry standards?
In the last 2 years, did the CA Owner meet every required revocation timeline (no misses)?
Does the CA Owner maintain documented incident-response procedures for mass-revocation events?
Can the CA Owner complete implementation of an emergency security change in production within 72 hours?
Does the CA Owner test all configuration changes in a staging environment before deploying to production?
Does the CA Owner have a standing body that authorizes its response to industry and standards changes and records those decisions in retrievable minutes?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented change-management process with documented rollback procedures for failed changes?
Does the CA Owner operate a staging or test infrastructure that closely mirrors production and is available to all Subscribers?
Does the CA Owner publish a public-facing changelog or release notes for policy and technical changes affecting Subscribers?
Does the CA Owner notify all Subscribers of upcoming changes at least 90 days in advance through a documented mechanism (such as a mailing list, notification service, or in-product alerting)?
Do Subscriber Agreements require Subscribers to protect private keys and to request revocation if key compromise is suspected?
Does the CA Owner verify that Subscriber contact information remains current at least annually?
Does the CA Owner maintain at least two distinct contact methods per Subscriber?
Does the CA Owner maintain a documented process for handling bounced communications to Subscribers?
Has the CA Owner operated a Certificate Transparency log qualified in Apple at any point in the past 2 years?
Is the CA Owner a member of the CA/Browser Forum?
Has the CA Owner authored or co-authored at least one CA/B Forum ballot in the past 2 years?
Has the CA Owner identified named personnel responsible for tracking CA/B Forum, CCADB, Root Program, IETF, (CT Program when applicable), and audit-standard updates?

Does the CA Owner operate a documented Subscriber-feedback process for proposed industry changes (including survey and intake), and share Subscriber feedback with relevant standards bodies (such as CA/B Forum or IETF) when participating in standards development?
Has the CA Owner read at least 50% of public incident reports owned by other CA Owners in the past 2 years?
Has the CA Owner read all public incident reports owned by other CA Owners in the past 2 years?

Has the CA Owner made at least one substantive, attributable contribution in the past 2 years to PKI-ecosystem tooling that benefits the community (for example a certificate linter, an ACME client, a certificate-monitoring service, or weak-key detection), with verifiable evidence?
Has the CA Owner attended (in-person or virtual) at least 50% of CA/B Forum Face-to-Face meetings in the past 2 years?
Is the CA Owner free of any removal, blocklisting, or constraint imposed by Apple or another CCADB Steering Committee member? (Not counting constraints it requested itself.)

Is the CA Owner free of any affiliation (organizational, financial, or operational) with a CA Owner that Apple or another CCADB Steering Committee member has removed, blocklisted, or constrained? (Constraints the CA Owner requested itself do not count.)

Is the CA Owner free of any affiliation (organizational, financial, or operational) with a government or vendor that has used CA certificates to intercept network traffic, surveil end users, or force Root CA certificate installation?
Does the CA Owner avoid using shell companies, holding companies, or other corporate-structure obfuscation to mask relationships with other organizations or governments?
Are at least 75% of personnel operating the CA full-time employees of the CA Owner?
In the past 5 years, has the CA Owner had no personal-data breaches?

Does the CA Owner log all TLS certificates (as precertificates) to at least one Apple-qualified CT log and embed at least the Apple-minimum number of SCTs in the final certificate (or N/A if the CA Owner does not issue TLS)?
Do all TLS subscriber certificates have a maximum domain-validation reuse period of 30 days or less (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Do all TLS subscriber certificates have a maximum domain-validation reuse period of 90 days or less (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Do all TLS subscriber certificates have a maximum validity of 90 days or less (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Do all TLS subscriber certificates have a maximum validity of 45 days or less (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Does the CA Owner issue Short-Lived TLS certificates with maximum validity of 10 days or less (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?

Is the CA Owner's ACME issuance available to public Subscribers without requiring a paid contract or out-of-band credential provisioning (functional External Account Binding) (or N/A if the CA Owner does not issue TLS)?
Do at least 75% of all TLS Subscriber certificates issued by the CA Owner use automated issuance and renewal (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Do at least 50% of all TLS Subscriber certificates issued by the CA Owner use automated issuance and renewal (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?
Does the CA Owner support the ACME protocol for TLS Subscriber certificate issuance and renewal (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?

Has the CA Owner attended at least 50% of SCWG meetings in the past 2 years (or N/A if not issuing TLS)?

Do all S/MIME subscriber certificates have a maximum validity of 397 days or less (or N/A if not issuing S/MIME)?
